Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
A few quick questions on what is considered the "same card."

Specialization [BH:R]
Cardtype: Master
Unique master.
Put this card in play. During your untap phase, you may tap this card and
discard two copies of the same card from your hand to gain 1 pool. Draw back up
to your hand size afterward.

#1. Do cards that have undergone spelling changes still count as the same card?
Take Heidelberg vs. Heidelburg or Trick of Danya vs. Trick of the Danya. I
would assume so since NRA considers both Tricks to be the same card.

#2. Are Stake and Wooden Stake considered to be different cards? I would assume
so (so you could also equip a Stake and also equip a Wooden Stake in the same
turn without violating NRA). This might be more likely to happen now that the
Grouping rule for Limited Tournaments has been lifted (so playing Jyhad and
VTES with Black Hand isn't entirely unfeasible).

#3. Similarly, how about Gangrel Atavism and Gangrel De-Evolution? I would
assume they are different cards as well.

Just wanted to check. Thanks!

Halcyan 2

If it's the same card, it's the same card. Variant spellings and renamings
of the same card do not count as different cards.

Stake and Wooden Stake are two names for the same card.
Same with Gangrel Atavism and Gangrel De-Evolution.

See online card lists for those and other such renamings.

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson

On Sun, 21 Dec 2003 10:35:52 -0500, LSJ wrote:

>If it's the same card, it's the same card.

That's begging the question. This is not the policy when determining
the admissibility of cards from a new expansion, is it? The new
printing of a card is considered to be different from the old,
regardless of whether they have the same text or effect. So,
arguably, just being from different expansions is enough to make two
versions of a card not the same.

Andrew

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
Andrew S. Davidson <a...@csi.com> wrote in message news:<r77guv0v9t52a3io5...@4ax.com>...


You're comparing apples and oranges here. Whether or not a card is
'considered different from the old' in terms of printings and
tournament legality has nothing to do with whether or not a card is
considered different in terms of game play.

For instance, whether or not your card says "Jyhad" or "Vampire" on
the back has absolutely no meaning to play once a game has begun.
Similarly the expansion symbol has no meaning while you play, and
neither does if a card is WotC constructed-tournament-legal

The admissibility of cards from a new expansion is a deck-building
rule specific to WotC-sanctioned tournaments - nothing about the game
stops you from using a card that was released 2 days ago in friendly
play or in a tournament that you and your buddies run. It's
specifically a restriction about WotC tournaments, not about 'the
rules of the game of V:TES'.

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Andrew S. Davidson wrote:
> arguably, just being from different expansions is enough to make two
> versions of a card not the same.

Do follow the topic, won't you?

This thread, as indicated by the subject line and meticulously detailed
in Halcyan2's original post, is about what constitutes two copies of
the same card for the purposes of Specialization.

It is not about whether one card is the same as another for

* collecting (i.e., it is indistinguishable from the other)
* ownership (i.e., it is the same physical copy as the other)
* aesthetics (i.e., it has the same [name], art, and background as the other)
* set rotation (i.e., has the same [name], and expansion symbol or border)

A card is the "same" as another for the purposes of this thread if,
as previously indicated, it has the same name (after accounting for
variant spellings and renamings).

If one has a particular pair of cards in mind, then, as indicated, one
can check the online card lists to see if they share a single entry
(in which case they are the same card for game purposes).
